fields.why: Period contrasts (percent change, VRs with CIs) are computed separately within females and males, which is literally 'a comparison within levels of a third variable' (A); B's reading under 'a series over time by group is a comparison, not stratification' is also defensible. A is slightly preferred because explicit period contrasts, not just a time series, are estimated within sex strata.
The drug overdose outcome is defined as 'acute drug poisonings' and suicide-related behaviors include self-harm, so injury/poisoning applies alongside substance use; A missed it.

The Discussion names social and structural factors as possible explanations of the trends (return to school/community environments, isolation, adverse childhood experiences, federal investment in the 988 line and telehealth access); the brief records determinants even below level 4 and excludes only unmeasured confounders and recommendations.

brief_issues: Brief should say whether period contrasts computed within sex (or other) strata count as stratified or fall under 'series over time by group'. B's merged record keeps the structural note 'stratified/adjusted is recorded on that basis' after the review removed it: merge leaves stale notes. Readers also differ on role (A primary, B ancillary) for VR CI-vs-1; headline claims rest on percent-change thresholds, so ancillary looks better, but role is not in the disagreement set.
